'''Progressive Sealed Deck''' is a sealed deck format in which each player's deck grows during the tournament. [[Decipher]] ran it as a side event at [[DecipherCon 1999]] for Star Wars CCG and ''Star Trek'' CCG. Decipher's own description of the event is not preserved; the only account of its rules is [[Martin Akesson]]'s: play started "with the sealed box, and then you got a new hope booster after each game to boost your deck".<ref name="tr-d163">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ world-championships-by-martin-akesson], DeckTech (Martin "Mart" Akesson, 9 January 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009094534/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-01-09-world-championships-by-martin-akessond163/ Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="dc99-thu">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/thu_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule: Thursday], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000122035723/http://decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/thu_events.html Internet Archive]</ref>

* '''Type:''' sealed deck
* '''Defined by:''' Decipher (1999)
* '''Card pool:''' a sealed product ("the sealed box"), plus an [[A New Hope]] booster added after each game (per Akesson's report)
* '''In use:''' 1999 (DecipherCon 1999)
* '''GEMP:''' none

== Card pool ==
Martin Akesson, who won the Star Wars event, wrote: "The fist day of the convention was a progressive sealed deck, starting with the sealed box, and then you got a new hope booster after each game to boost your deck."<ref name="tr-d163" /> He does not say which sealed product "the sealed box" was, how large decks had to be, or how many games were played.

Decipher's score sheets show 5 games on one sheet and 4 on the other. On both, every player played the same side of the Force in every game, as in an ordinary sealed deck event.<ref name="dc99sw22_1">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW22_1.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: Progressive Sealed Deck], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000525001947/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW22_1.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dc99sw22_2">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW22_2.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Scores: Progressive Sealed Deck], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001101003044/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/scores/SW22_2.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== History ==
DecipherCon 1999 scheduled the Star Wars Progressive Sealed Deck (event SW.22) on Thursday 11 November, 2 p.m.&ndash;8 p.m., Friday 12 November, 1 p.m.&ndash;7 p.m., and Saturday 13 November, 7 a.m.&ndash;1 p.m. The ''Star Trek'' CCG schedule had its own Progressive Sealed Deck (ST.22) on Friday and Saturday.<ref name="dc99-thu" /><ref name="dc99-fri">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/fri_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule: Friday], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000708001407/http://decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/fri_events.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dc99-sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sat_events.html DecipherCon 1999 – Event Schedule: Saturday], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20001026023004/http://decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/events/sat_events.html Internet Archive]</ref> The schedule linked each event title to a description page (progressivesealed.html), but no copy of that page is preserved.<ref name="dc99-fri" />

Akesson wrote that he won the event, with Darth Vader, Tarkin and TIEs in his deck, beating [[Aldrin Long]] in the final.<ref name="tr-d163" /> Results are on [[DecipherCon 1999 Progressive Sealed Deck]].
